limitations: PhysX contacts are not MuJoCo contacts: rigid Coulomb contacts with the max friction of the pair.  With contact='compliant' the roller/terrain pair becomes a PhysX compliant contact with the declared roller stiffness and damping per contact point; that option has not been exercised on any PhysX.

A roller is the union of convex hulls of neighbouring profile rings (PhysX limits a hull to 64 vertices).  The hull points are authored in millimetres under a 0.001 scale: PhysX convex cooking drops points closer than 0.0007 mesh units (0.7 mm on a mesh in metres) to the hull built so far, which would coarsen a 22 mm roller.
A compliant roller stiffness acts per contact point, so the wheel as a whole is stiffer than one such spring; every run reports the base height against rigid wheels.

There is no latch constraint and no force/torque sensor in the scene: the clamp is the compliant clamp of backends/latch.py applied by the runner, and the wrist sensor is the Newton-Euler balance of the tool-side body.
No joint drives, no PhysX joint friction and no rigid-body damping are authored; the declared joint damping is applied by the runner as an explicit effort.
Authored mass properties and joint frames are audited offline; what PhysX does with them is checked by the preflight of the Isaac Sim workflow (property readback, kinematics, free-flight dynamics).
